title: Projective presentation and affine coordinate charts of a homogeneous polynomial quotient
statement: Let $U$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $n\geq0$, and $\mathcal S=\mathcal O_U[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ with each variable of degree one. Let $J\subseteq\mathcal S$ be a quasi-coherent homogeneous ideal (the direct sum of its homogeneous pieces), locally generated by finitely many homogeneous sections, and put $\mathcal B=\mathcal S/J$ with its quotient grading. Quasi-coherence and graded algebra sheaves are as in [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. Let $Z=\operatorname{Proj}_U\mathcal B$ [def-nagata-relative-proj] and $\pi:Z\to U$ be its structure morphism. The quotient map induces a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-relative-projective-space], over $U$, under the canonical chart-compatible identification of the polynomial relative Proj with projective space [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. The morphism $\pi$ is projective [def-kun-projective] and proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and is finitely presented, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq U$, put $J_V=\Gamma(V,J)$ and $B=R[x_0,\ldots,x_n]/J_V$. The canonical maps identify $\Gamma(V,\mathcal B_d)$ with $B_d$ for every $d\geq0$ and identify $\pi^{-1}V$ with $\operatorname{Proj}B$. Writing $\bar x_i$ for the image of $x_i$, these identifications give a finite affine open cover $\pi^{-1}V=\bigcup_{i=0}^nD_+(\bar x_i)$, where $D_+(\bar x_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{(\bar x_i),0})$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. This includes degree-zero equations in $J$, the unit ideal, and zero or nilpotent $\bar x_i$ (whose charts are empty).

proof.text: First identify the polynomial algebra sheaf with the symmetric algebra of the free module $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(n+1)}$. The universal property and affine-section comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra], followed by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial], identify its sections on $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$. These maps send the distinguished basis sections to the variables. They preserve degrees, for the symmetric grading of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]: products of $d$ basis sections go to monomials of total degree $d$, and the inverse sends each variable to its basis section. Thus $\mathcal S$ is quasi-coherent and the identification is graded, with its usual coefficient map from $R$.

source.place: Tags 01CG (lemma-local-tensor-algebra), 01CL (lemma-whole-tensor-algebra-permanence); algebra.tex Section 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), finite free symmetric algebra paragraph

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] to $J\hookrightarrow\mathcal S$. It gives quasi-coherence of $\mathcal B$ and a surjection $\mathcal S(V)\to\mathcal B(V)$ with kernel $J(V)$ on every affine $V$. The resulting quotient identification is an algebra identification: products and units descend from the same sheaf algebra quotient. The homogeneous summands of $\mathcal S,J,\mathcal B$ are quasi-coherent: each is the image of its degree projection on the corresponding quasi-coherent total module, so use the image clause of the same node. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-evaluation] to their coproduct diagrams indexed by the small discrete category $\mathbb N$. Their cocone points are the quasi-coherent total modules just identified. Sections therefore preserve these direct sums. The section quotient is graded, and its degree-$d$ component is precisely $\Gamma(V,\mathcal B_d)=B_d$. The maps commute with affine restriction because they are the section maps of the given quotient and degree projections. In degree zero the coefficient map is $R\to R/(J_V)_0$, not necessarily an isomorphism.

Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] to $\mathcal B$. Step 2 identifies its affine model with $\operatorname{Proj}B$ over $V$, including the coefficient map through $B_0$. In $B$, every positive-degree homogeneous element has a homogeneous polynomial lift; every monomial in such a lift is divisible by some $x_i$. Hence the ideal generated by $\bar x_0,\ldots,\bar x_n$ contains the irrelevant ideal $B_+$. The covering and affine-chart assertions of [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] now give $\pi^{-1}V=\bigcup_{i=0}^nD_+(\bar x_i)$ and $D_+(\bar x_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{(\bar x_i),0})$. This is a finite cover with $n+1$ indices, without any requirement that its members be nonempty.

Here is the polynomial-Proj comparison with the base-change projective space. Put $F=\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(n+1)}$ with ordered basis $e_0,\ldots,e_n$. By Step 1, $\mathcal S$ is identified with $\operatorname{Sym}(F)$ by a degree-preserving algebra isomorphism that is the identity of $\mathcal O_U$ in degree zero and sends $x_i$ to $j_F(e_i)$. Clause 2 of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] turns it into an isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}_U\mathcal S\cong\operatorname{Proj}_U\operatorname{Sym}(F)$ over $U$, compatible with the affine restriction identifications of its clause 1. Apply [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] with $S=U$ and $r=n$: it gives the canonical isomorphism $\theta:\operatorname{Proj}_U\operatorname{Sym}(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};U)=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$ onto the projective space of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with $q\circ\theta=p$ for the two projections. Over every affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ its restriction is the Proj comparison induced by the graded $R$-algebra isomorphism $\operatorname{Sym}_R(R^{\oplus(n+1)})\cong R[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$, $\iota(e_i)\mapsto T_i$, and these local comparisons agree with restriction on the base. The composite of the two isomorphisms is the canonical chart-compatible identification of $\operatorname{Proj}_U\mathcal S$ with projective space used in the statement; it lies over $U$. No flatness of $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is used.

The quotient $\mathcal S\to\mathcal B$ is a surjective degree-preserving morphism of quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_U$-algebras. The surjection clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] therefore induces a closed immersion $Z\to\operatorname{Proj}_U\mathcal S$ over $U$. Compose with the chart-compatible isomorphism of Step 4. This is the claimed quotient-induced closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_U$, and its composite with the projection is $\pi$. This factorization supplies projectivity exactly as defined in [def-kun-projective], with $N=n$.

By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], the projective map $\pi$ is proper. Its definition [def-weil-proper-morphism] supplies separatedness and finite type, and finite type means locally finite type and quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $U$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] applies to $\pi$ and gives local finite presentation. Its separatedness implies quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. The three conditions just obtained are precisely finite presentation in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. This uses no quasi-compactness assumption on the entire base $U$.

proof.text: The argument also checks the degenerate cases. Degree-zero relations only replace the coefficient ring in Step 2 by $B_0$; no step asserted $B_0=R$. If $J=\mathcal S$, then $B=0$ and every displayed chart is empty. If $\bar x_i$ is zero or nilpotent, inverting it gives the zero ring: from $\bar x_i^e=0$ and its invertibility one gets $1=0$. Consequently its degree-zero localization in [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] is the zero ring, so its spectrum is empty. The monomial covering argument still holds; in particular $n=0$, the empty base and an entirely empty relative Proj are all included.
